answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a marble as the anchor of the cost. A kernel stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a thread...
